problem: Suppose $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(A)=-63.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{2}{9}{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$

feedback.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=2.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\frac{3}{2}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =\frac{3}{2}det(A) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
